rationale: Response A is more complete and execution-ready: it connects audience journeys to messaging, channel selection, content planning, launch-day sequencing, risk management, measurement, testing, and formal readiness review, with clear deliverables and facilitation methods throughout. Response B has valuable additions—especially engineering participation, audience validation, a pre-mortem, and explicit tracking methods—but its advertised 3–3.5-hour workshops contain only about 2–2.3 hours of activities, leaving the agenda materially underspecified, and its page-by-page content-gap exercise drifts somewhat from launch communications into website production. A also has minor timing inconsistencies, but its overall workshop architecture is deeper and more actionable.
